title: Adoption Plan Prioritizer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Ordering activity in which learners arrange six steps for adopting AI research practices in a group (lab AI policy, shared repository, pilot skill, verification checks, agent team, 90-day review), shown in a scrambled order, into a sequence that respects five dependencies. A submission is reported as a valid order with the dependency list, or the first violated dependency is named with its reason; both valid orders and the dependency graph are then shown. Only the first submission counts as evidence; later submissions are practice.

educational.topic: Staged adoption of AI research practices in a research group
learningObjectives: Prioritize six adoption steps for a research group into an order that respects their dependencies, and state the dependency that justifies each constraint
Recognize that the lab AI policy and the shared repository may be done in either order, because both are prerequisites only of the pilot
prerequisites: Lab AI policy, project instruction file, pilot skill, verification checks, review gates, and agent team, from earlier chapters
The section Adopting These Practices in Chapter 20

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; the step choice is a native select element and every action is a native HTML button that responds to the Tab key and Enter or Space, so ordering never needs dragging; valid and invalid feedback uses words and check or cross symbols as well as an Okabe-Ito blue and vermillion palette, and the broken dependency is drawn as a dashed arrow; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Pick a step / Step A to Step F
controls.purpose: Chooses one of the six steps to move. Each option shows the step's current position, for example Step C (#4). The picked step is outlined on the canvas.

controls.label: Earlier
controls.purpose: Moves the picked step one position earlier. Disabled when the step is first.

controls.label: Later
controls.purpose: Moves the picked step one position later. Disabled when the step is last.

controls.label: Submit Order
controls.purpose: Checks the sequence. Reports Valid order or the first violated dependency with its reason, then shows both valid orders and the dependency graph. Only the first submission counts as evidence.

controls.label: Next Page
controls.purpose: Shown only when the feedback does not fit. Pages through the feedback; on narrow screens it also moves between the step view and the feedback pages.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Prioritization task with a dependency check, a reason for the first violated dependency, and a revealed dependency graph with both valid orders
keyQuestions: Which steps must come first, and why?
What must be in place before a pilot touches real data?
Why must the checks exist before a team is scaled?
commonMisconceptions: Start with the most capable agents and add controls later
Policy can be written after the pilot
Scaling is the first step after a pilot
assessmentOpportunities: A valid order on the first submission is evidence of mastery
Reading the step descriptions and later practice submissions are exploration and are not evidence
